title: `Environment` ambient light is not affected by `CameraAttributes` exposure
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.0.stable.official [92bee43ad] - Reproducible in v4.5.stable.official [876b29033] Reproducible with Forward+, Mobile, and Compatibility. ### System information Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8108) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads) - 63.74 GiB memory ### Issue description Changing `CameraAttributes` exposure settings does not affect ambient light from the `Environment` when the ambient light source is either `Color` or `Background` when Background mode is `Color`. Specifically, if the `CameraAttributes` exposure multiplier is set to `0.0` and there is ambient light (source: color or background color), the image is not black: This issue does not seem to present itself when the ambient light source is set to `Sky` or `Background` when Background mode is `Sky`. It happens with and without physical light units with both `CameraAttributesPractical` or `CameraAttributesPhysical`. ### Fog It seems that the same issue happens with the Fog environment effect, but not with Volumetric fog. I suspect there is a fair bit of review and testing of all of the features of Godot to fully resolve this issue... ### Expected behaviour: I would expect the `CameraAttributes` exposure to produce the same image as the tonemap exposure setting. I believe the only difference between these two exposure settings is that tonemap exposure can be applied to canvas items (via Background mode: Canvas), while CameraAttributes exposure cannot. Please correct me if my expectation is incorrect! ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a 3D scene with a world environment 2. Set the ambient light source to Color and change the color to be non-black 3. Add a `CameraAttributes` to the environment 4. Change exposure settings 5. Note that ambient light appears unaffected. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [camera-attributes-ambient-light.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22729380/camera-attributes-ambient-light.zip)
